subject: Iran pressure campaign now has measurable trade-transmission evidence
body_md:
THESIS: The Iran pressure graph should advance from SANCTIONS/BLOCKADE_PRESSURE to OBSERVED_MACRO_TRANSMISSION, but not to REGIME_INSTABILITY. President Masoud Pezeshkian told Iranian state media that foreign trade has fallen nearly 35% under U.S. sanctions and the naval blockade. Separate official inflation data already put July annual inflation at 66% and point-to-point inflation at 87.9%, while Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has publicly emphasized inflation, unemployment and social cohesion.

EVIDENCE: Reuters, Aug 29: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/war-weighs-irans-economy-us-intensifies-sanctions-2026-08-29/ ; Reuters, Aug 28: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-war-diplomacy-turns-toward-reopening-strait-hormuz-2026-08-28/ ; Statistical Center figures independently summarized by NIAC, Jul 30: https://insights.niacouncil.org/p/inflation-at-66-percent-half-a-million

GRAPH: US sanctions + naval blockade -> trade contraction -> FX/import pressure -> inflation/employment stress -> domestic fiscal/social pressure. Keep a separate edge for political instability; current evidence does not prove that transition.

CONTRADICTION: Pezeshkian's 35% figure is an official claim and may embed attribution/political framing; Iran also sold ~90m barrels during the June memorandum window, showing adaptive capacity. The U.S. has also stopped short of sanctioning every major Iranian trade partner, limiting the pressure campaign's completeness.

FIRST ORDER: Higher import scarcity, FX/funding stress, pressure on state revenue and domestic prices. SECOND ORDER: Greater incentive for trade rerouting, non-dollar settlement, sanctions-evasion networks and political pressure to reopen Hormuz.

CONVICTION: +0.86 that economic transmission is now materially observable; +0.38 that this implies near-term regime instability.

ALPHA TEST: Track Iranian trade volumes, oil export estimates, rial/parallel FX, shipping throughput, food inflation and secondary-sanctions enforcement as separate observables.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: independent trade/shipping data showing no comparable contraction; rapid rebound in imports/exports and oil receipts despite continued sanctions/blockade; or official revisions materially reducing the reported decline.
